decisions.review_reason: All 301 distinct Nicotinic acid descriptors were inspected with reconstruction-verified factoring, including every source qualifier and evidence text. MediaDive, JCM, DSMZ, TOGO, KOMODO and BacDive labels preserve the neutral acid name; no salt or nicotinate identity is substituted. Stock/batch quantities, historical duplicate sums and inferred denominators remain separate and are not approved.

All six lowercase nicotinic-acid descriptors were read. The primary yeast-paper excerpts explicitly restore nicotinic acid despite historical MediaDB Nicotinate labels; the remaining descriptors preserve the acid name. The neutral owner matches without accepting historical cross-reference identities or certifying doses.

The inspected MediaDive2006 descriptor explicitly preserves Nicotinate and CHEBI32544, which live ChEBI defines as the conjugate-base anion. The native owner CHEBI15940 is neutral nicotinic acid. Its exact synonym alone does not resolve supplied-form identity for the complete case.

blocking_witnesses.reason: Explicit CHEBI32544 nicotinate anion conflicts with native neutral nicotinic acid CHEBI15940; source form remains unresolved.

decisions.review_reason: All18 Nicotinic Acid descriptors retain the neutral acid, including CAS59-67-6 and Wolfe/Thauer/CCAP stock contexts. The owner matches the named solute; DL vitamins is retained as a stock name rather than stereochemistry, and no stock formulation or dose is approved.

All16 Niacin descriptors and MediaDive610 source excerpts were inspected. They preserve the chemical niacin/nicotinic-acid name used by this owner, with no nicotinamide or salt qualifier. Named stocks and quantities remain explicit; this does not generalize vitaminB3 activity into chemical equivalence.

The sole lowercase niacin descriptor preserves the same nicotinic-acid chemical name and no contradictory material qualifier. Binding the owner does not certify the legacy50g/L quantity or vitamin efficacy.

All three Nitrate descriptors preserve the bare nitrate-anion name, including MediaDB287 and KEGGno3 context. Live ChEBI17632 confirms this anion concept. No supplied salt, actual solution speciation or quantitative validity is inferred.

The complete held mention explicitly retains IDENTITY_FORM and OPERATION uncertainty: nitrate absence describes a separate BG110 comparator, not a removal from the nitrate-replete BG11 variant. Its source does not establish a specific nitrate material or operational event; preserve the held case.

blocking_witnesses.reason: The source describes nitrate absence in a separate BG110 comparator and explicitly leaves identity/form and operational membership unresolved.

decisions.review_reason: The sole source explicitly names nitrilotriacetic acid trisodium salt. The reviewed native owner preserves three sodium ions per NTA and distinguishes disodium stock history; this matches the named salt without adding hydration or approving concentration.

Both N2O descriptors preserve the nitrous-oxide formula, matching the native molecular owner. Their legacy percent-w/v gas quantities are not approved or converted; no nitric oxide or nitrogen dioxide identity is substituted.
The sole descriptor names N2O and explicitly retains gas/variable-amount context. Nitrous oxide matches the owner; unspecified dosage and gas handling remain outside this identity binding.

The complete Carini2014 REPLACE payload preserves O-phospho-L-serine only as the displaced inherited parent label. That historical context label matches the owner; the new source phosphoserine remains stereochemically unspecified. This does not assert L reagent presence or establish the inherited base recipe experimentally.

The positive AMS1 parent descriptor inherits O-phospho-L-serine and KEGG:pser-L, but the same recipe's primary-source-bound replacement explicitly records that Carini2014 does not establish D/L stereochemistry. Preserve the unresolved supplied-material specificity rather than promote the inherited L annotation.

blocking_witnesses.reason: Inherited L-specific positive descriptor lacks primary stereochemical support; the same recipe's exact reviewed replacement event explicitly records the paper's unspecified D/L form.

decisions.review_reason: Both descriptors explicitly name OADC Enrichment, matching the maintained local named-preparation owner. It remains an opaque multicomponent stock; no fixed formulation, equivalence to an individual constituent, or inconsistent mass/volume dose is approved.

All nine Oat flakes descriptors and DSMZ189/1815, MediaDive512/316/855/425 source contexts preserve the flaked oat preparation. The FOODON material matches without substituting oatmeal powder or approving dose and extraction yield.

Source Quaker White Oats is retained as a brand-qualified oatmeal ingredient in JCM50/148 and TOGO M42. Live NCITC29298 instead denotes colloidal oatmeal milled to fine powder. The actual source does not independently establish that processing scope; a synonym cannot bridge it.

blocking_witnesses.reason: Brand-qualified Quaker White Oats does not establish the colloidal fine-powder preparation required by NCITC29298.

decisions.review_reason: The aggregate case includes unqualified Oatmeal with no powder/colloidal preparation evidence, while NCITC29298 explicitly denotes finely milled colloidal oatmeal. Other descriptors saying powdered do not establish every source member's preparation; preserve the complete case pending source-specific resolution.

blocking_witnesses.reason: Unqualified oatmeal does not independently establish the narrower colloidal fine-powder preparation in NCITC29298.

decisions.review_reason: The TOGO M2407 OADC stock descriptor explicitly names Oleic Acid. The neutral oleic-acid owner matches the named input, not the entire enrichment; the volume-only dose and absent final denominator remain separate.
Both descriptors explicitly name9Z-octadecenoic acid, preserving the cis9 geometry of oleic acid. The owner matches without accepting a different geometric isomer or certifying the molar quantities.

All16 Oleic acid descriptors and complete DSMZ645/911, KOMODO and TOGO OADC source excerpts were inspected. They preserve the named neutral acid; stock composition, volume-only inputs, provider rates and final-medium doses remain separate and receive no new quantity or growth approval.

All seven Olive oil descriptors preserve the named food oil across NBRC103, JCM188 and MediaDive3848/6326. The generic olive-oil material matches; no purity grade, triglyceride composition, mass-volume conversion or dose is inferred.

The sole Orotate descriptor retains the bare anion name and KEGGorot context. Live ChEBI30839 confirms the orotate anion distinct from orotic acid. This binds the maintained concept without selecting a salt or approving actual solution protonation or concentration.

All six Orotic acid descriptors retain the neutral acid, including CAS65-86-1 in Soil Defined Carbon Mix and Northen stocks and CCAP UCM context. The acid owner matches without substituting orotate or approving stock doses.

All three Orthophosphate descriptors retain the bare orthophosphate name in MediaDB287/37/36. Live ChEBI18367 lists Orthophosphate as the named phosphate-anion concept. Binding this maintained concept does not establish the supplied salt, actual solution protonation, medium pH, or the legacy quantities.

Both Ox-bile descriptors retain bovine bile material, including MediaDive502. The native MICRO owner explicitly preserves the compositionally variable bile preparation. No fixed chemical composition, specific processing subtype, or amount is inferred.

Both p-hydroxybenzyl-alcohol descriptors retain the para substitution, independently named in the primary Table2 excerpt for MediaDB466/441. The owner matches that neutral alcohol, without approving inherited dose, entire cobalt-variant composition or growth.
